topic: Sarnath: India's 45th UNESCO World Heritage Site

subtopics.title: Inscription and India's World Heritage status
subtopics.summary: Sarnath was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List at the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee, held in Busan, Republic of Korea. With this inscription India has 45 World Heritage Sites, ranking 6th globally and 2nd in the Asia-Pacific region. Of these sites, 37 are cultural, 7 are natural and 1 is mixed.
facts: Inscribed during the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee in Busan (Republic of Korea)
With Sarnath, India now has 45 UNESCO World Heritage Sites
India ranks 6th globally and 2nd in the Asia-Pacific region
India's sites: 37 Cultural, 7 Natural, 1 Mixed
Khangchendzonga National Park (Sikkim) is India's mixed heritage site
1983 inscriptions: Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Ajanta and Ellora Caves
Dholavira (Gujarat) is the only Indus Valley Civilization site from India on the list
India hosted the 46th Annual Session at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi
India served as a Committee Member for the 2021-2025 term

subtopics.title: Sarnath's sites and the first sermon
subtopics.summary: Sarnath is where Gautama Buddha gave his first sermon after attaining enlightenment at Bodhgaya, an event known as Dharmachakra Pravartana. The site has ancient names including Rishipatana, Ishipatana and Mrigadava. Its archaeological features include several stupas, a vihara and the Ashokan Pillar, each associated with a particular event or ruler.
facts: Ancient names: Rishipatana, Ishipatana and Mrigadava (Deer Park)
Buddha gave his first sermon at Sarnath after enlightenment at Bodhgaya

The sermon marks the beginning of the Buddhist Sangha
Chaukhandi Stupa: meeting of Buddha and his first five disciples
Dhamekh Stupa: marks the site of Buddha's first sermon
Dharmarajika Stupa: traditionally associated with Emperor Ashoka and Buddha's relics
Mulagandhakuti Vihara: Buddha's rainy-season retreat at Sarnath
Ashokan Pillar: erected during Ashoka's reign; its Lion Capital is India's National Emblem
Sarnath is one of 4 principal Buddhist pilgrimage sites (with Lumbini, Bodhgaya, Kushinagar)

subtopics.title: UNESCO, the Convention and the recognition process
subtopics.summary: The World Heritage List is maintained by the World Heritage Programme and administered by the UNESCO World Heritage Committee. The Convention concerning Protection of World Cultural and Natural Heritage was adopted in 1972, took effect in 1975, and was ratified by India in 1977. In India the Archaeological Survey of India is the nodal agency, while ICOMOS and IUCN carry out the assessment before the Committee takes the final decision.
facts: UNESCO was founded in 1945; its headquarters are in Paris, France
UNESCO stands for United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization

subtopics.title: Gautama Buddha and Buddhism
subtopics.summary: Gautama Buddha was born as Siddhartha in 563 BC at Lumbini, near Kapilavastu, and died at Kushinagara in 487 BC. He taught the Middle Path, the Four Noble Truths and the 8-Fold Path, and he called himself Tathagata. After his death his teachings were divided into three Pitakas at the First Buddhist Council.
facts: Born as Siddhartha in 563 BC at Lumbini (Nepal), near Kapilavastu
Father was an elected ruler of Kapilvastu and headed the Shakya republican clan
Mother was a princess from the Koshalan dynasty
Death (Mahaparinirvana) at Kushinagara in 487 BC
Referred to himself as Tathagata (one who has thus come or gone)
Buddhism based on his teachings, developed in the 6th century BC
Buddhism rejects the authority of the Vedas and the concept of soul (atman)
Middle Path (Madhyam Marg): avoid the extremes
Four Noble Truths: suffering, its cause, its ending, and the path to ending it
8-Fold Path: right view, intention, speech, action, livelihood, mindfulness, effort, concentration

The Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath has been inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. A World Heritage Site is a place that UNESCO has listed for its cultural or physical significance. The list is maintained by the World Heritage Programme and administered by the UNESCO World Heritage Committee, which meets in annual sessions.

Sarnath is where Gautama Buddha delivered his first sermon after attaining enlightenment at Bodhgaya. The event marks the beginning of the Buddhist Sangha and is associated with the establishment of the Noble Eightfold Path. Sarnath is also one of four principal Buddhist pilgrimage sites, along with Lumbini, Bodhgaya and Kushinagar.

The site contains several archaeological features. The Chaukhandi Stupa is associated with the meeting of Buddha and his first five disciples, while the Dharmarajika Stupa is traditionally linked with Emperor Ashoka and Buddha's relics. The Mulagandhakuti Vihara is associated with Buddha's rainy-season retreat.

The list classifies sites as cultural, natural or mixed, and India has a mixed heritage site. India has also hosted an annual session of the World Heritage Committee. Each proposal is assessed by expert bodies before the Committee decides. With Sarnath's inscription, the list now includes one more Indian place. The Committee is the body that makes the final decision on each site.

quizzes.passage:
UNESCO is an organisation that works in education, science and culture. Among its programmes is the World Heritage Programme, which maintains the World Heritage List. A place on that list is one that UNESCO has recognised for its cultural or physical significance. Sites recognised under the list are described as World Heritage Sites.

The rules for this recognition are set out in an international treaty called the Convention concerning Protection of World Cultural and Natural Heritage. Countries join the treaty through ratification, and India is one of the countries that has done so. The World Heritage Committee administers the list, while the treaty embodies the recognition process itself.

Sites on the list fall into several categories, including cultural, natural and mixed sites. Before a site is added, it is reviewed by expert organisations, and the process ends with a final stage. The list sits alongside other UNESCO efforts, such as the Memory of the World Register, the Man and Biosphere Programme and Intangible Cultural Heritage.

The Convention names both cultural and natural heritage in its title, which is why the list covers both kinds of places. UNESCO's full name, United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization, reflects its work in these three fields.

UNESCO is an organisation that works in education, science and culture, and its name reflects these three fields. The World Heritage List is maintained by the World Heritage Programme, and places on the list are recognised for their cultural or physical significance.

The List is based on an international treaty known as the Convention concerning Protection of World Cultural and Natural Heritage. Countries become party to the treaty through ratification. In India, a government body is the nodal agency for World Heritage matters.

Proposed sites go through a review by expert organisations before the final stage of recognition. The World Heritage Committee administers the list. Sites on the list fall into cultural, natural and mixed categories. Other UNESCO efforts include the Memory of the World Register, the Man and Biosphere Programme and Intangible Cultural Heritage.

The World Heritage Committee is the body that takes decisions on the list, while the expert organisations provide assessments that inform those decisions. The recognition of a place on the list therefore rests on the treaty, the review by expert bodies and the Committee's decision. Sarnath's recent inscription followed this structure, which is the framework in which recognition operates. The list is maintained, and sites are recognised, under the framework described above.
